summary: Round 2 re-validation: all 3 Round 1 critical/major findings are resolved. Checked 42 claims against the live codebase. Found 1 new minor internal contradiction (Decision 1 alternative says hw_review.cmd_publish calls _fallback_publish, but it does not — Decision 5 correctly states the opposite). Round 1 minor line-number drift (1-4 lines) persists in a couple of spots but is non-blocking and the spec already explicitly notes 'around line X' or X+ semantics in those references.

findings.claim: Decision 1, Alternatives section (tech-spec line 75): '_fallback_publish is also called from hw_review.cmd_publish (live in code, see Decision 5); duplicating the guard at the slot level requires changes in two places. Function-level is the dominator.'
findings.reality: hw_review.cmd_publish (hw_review.py:569) does NOT call _fallback_publish. It has its own inline publish path (Telegraph create, mark_telegraph_published, send_telegraph_teaser, then move_to_published directly at hw_review.py:655). grep across hw_review.py shows ZERO calls to _fallback_publish — only one comment-string reference at hw_review.py:553. Decision 5 of THIS SAME tech-spec correctly says (line 106): 'hw_review.cmd_publish does NOT pass through _fallback_publish's guard (it has its own publish path)'. So the tech-spec contradicts itself: Decision 1 alt-rejected reasoning leans on a non-existent call site, while Decision 5 rationale leans on the correct fact (no shared call site).
findings.source: tech-spec.md, Decision 1 → Alternatives → 'Inside slot loop in job() (line 1733)' rejection rationale (line 75)
findings.fix: Reword the Decision 1 alternative rejection: the function-level guard is still the right architectural choice because (a) it sits BEFORE every path through _fallback_publish (outage shortcut + 3 Claude branches), and (b) future callers of _fallback_publish would inherit the guard for free without duplication. But DROP the false claim that hw_review.cmd_publish calls _fallback_publish today — it doesn't. Suggest: 'rejected — slot-level placement adds a redundant DB read per slot AND would not protect any future caller of _fallback_publish; function-level is the architectural dominator across the 4 internal paths (outage shortcut at 1045, Claude success at ~1056, per-article fallback at 1065, ClaudeOutageError at 1079).'

findings.claim: Multiple references in tech-spec cite Claude success at line 1052 (Architecture diagram line 52, Decision 1 rationale line 73, line 64 of Architecture summary).
findings.reality: transcreate_via_claude() is actually called at news_bot.py:1056 (the try-block opens at 1055, the call is at 1056). Drift = 4 lines. The except ClaudeTranscreationError line 1065 and except ClaudeOutageError line 1079 are exact. The is_fallback_active() shortcut line 1045 is exact. Spec uses '1052+' notation in the prose, which softens this, but the Architecture ASCII diagram and Decision 1 rationale state '1052' as if precise.
findings.source: tech-spec.md, Architecture diagram (line 52), Decision 1 rationale (line 73), Architecture summary (line 63-64)
findings.fix: Update '1052' references to '1056' (or keep '~1052' / 'around 1052' to acknowledge approximate). Non-blocking — the semantic point (Claude success path exists, dominator is upstream) is correct.
